samir: FYI: ran a nightly SLA perf job and saw a 15-22% regression on a bunch of customer workloads with head_dim=48 on L40s. autotuner now prefers sdpa_v1 fallback instead of v3 for causal paths :eyes:

anil: can you paste the autotune decision blob / config? curious which metric pushed it to v1

samir: pasted below — small excerpt from the decision dump:
```
model: r3-small
heads: 8
head_dim: 48
seq_len: 1024
batch: 1
causal: true
hw: nvidia-l40s
candidates: [sdpa_v3, sdpa_v2, sdpa_v1]
chosen: sdpa_v1
reason: latency_p99 slightly lower in microbench (with pad-to-64)
```

tess: interesting — pad-to-64 changing microbench results makes sense. Are we autotuning on padded synthetic inputs? if so that can bias kernels that vectorize better with padding

samir: yes the microbench pads to 64 for alignment. but the actual runtime path doesn't pad; it streams kv-cache with head_dim remainder handling, so v3 was faster in end-to-end traces previously

maria: any flamegraphs / nvprof snapshots? curious where cycles go (bank conflicts? swizzle?)

ci-bot: perf artifacts uploaded: https://ci.internal.redwood/perf/1845678901/artifacts (nvprof trace, scc, autotune-blob.json)

anil: looked at the nvprof — v1 picked has a lower compute kernel time for full-tile ops, but when kv-cache path hits the odd head remainder we pay ~extra memcpy and scalar tail loops. effect grows with seq_len because KV scatter/concat happens per step. that matches the 15-22%

anil: hypothesis: autotuner uses one-shot microbench after padding which favors kernels with larger vector widths. but runtime uses causal incremental KV updates that reveal head_dim % 32 != 0 tail penalties. we should weight the microbench with a kv-cache incremental testcase

samir: agreed. also saw divergence across microarchitectures — on ampere v3 beats v1 even with padding. on l40s the microbench numbers for v1 are slightly better due to different tensor core tile sizes

maria: can we add a hardware-aware penalty to candidate scoring? e.g., add a small tail-cost estimate when head_dim % warp != 0, and add a causality factor when causal=true (because incremental KV path matters)

anil: yeah we can model tail cost roughly as: tail_cost = (head_dim % vector_width) * per_elem_scalar_cost * seq_len * batch. add it to autotune score. also include a kv_update_multiplier when causal=true

samir: quick repro script if anyone wants to run locally:
```bash
# repro: 1-step forward with kv streaming
python - <<'PY'
import torch
from runtime import run_infer
model = 'r3-small'
opts = dict(heads=8, head_dim=48, seq_len=1024, batch=1, causal=True)
for kernel in ['sdpa_v3','sdpa_v2','sdpa_v1']:
    print(kernel, run_infer(model, kernel, **opts).p99())
PY
```

tess: opened draft PR with two fixes: 1) add kv-incremental microbench to autotune harness 2) add head-tail penalty term to scoring. PTAL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4832 :rocket:

anil: left a comment — we should also avoid pad-to-64 in the microbench by default. instead run two variants: padded and unpadded and combine scores (weighted by expected runtime pad-fraction).

samir: good. we should also add a regression test in perf CI: run seqlen=1..2048 with headdims [32,48,64,80] on representative hw images and fail if choose_v1 for causal head_dim with >10% regression vs median historical

maria: i'll add the perf CI job. tagging infra to spin up an L40s image in canary for the next nightly.

ci-bot: created issue #4829: "autotune: account for head-dim tails and kv-cache incremental cost" with links to traces and PRs

samir: assigning to @anil and @tess. thanks all. keeping this thread for followups. :thumbsup:
